newsitem.title: USA: US FCC chief sees comprehensive phone plan in May.
newsitem.headline: US FCC chief sees comprehensive phone plan in May.

text.p: The nation's top phone regulator said on Tuesday his agency would adopt a comprehensive plan early next month to keep phone service affordable for rural and low-income communities.

But Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt reiterated that the FCC will have to work with state regulators over the next year to determine the size of the fund needed to support universal service.
Speaking at Georgetown University, Hundt said the FCC's May 6 decision would be "on time and I hope on target."
The FCC "will deliver a detailed, comprehensive and complete decision to connect all the groups and locations Congress wants connected," he added.
Hundt said the FCC needs to work with the states to figure out the method for calculating the cost of the universal service fund.

"On a long-term basis, a sustainable national universal service plan requires coordination with the states and reaction to the unveiling of competition. For that reason, we intend over the course of the coming year to reconvene the federal-state univerasl service joint board," he said.
